title: API Key Is Empty Inside the Container
intro: The app crashes on startup with 'API_KEY is not set'. The developer insists they passed it: the Dockerfile has 'ARG API_KEY' and the build used '--build-arg API_KEY=abc123'.

steps.prompt: Check the container's logs to confirm the exact error.
steps.fake_output:
Error: API_KEY is not set
    at loadConfig (config.js:12)
steps.hint: Always confirm the exact error message before theorizing about causes.

steps.prompt: Check what environment variables are actually set inside the container at runtime.
steps.hint: Look for API_KEY in the list — is it there at all?

steps.prompt: API_KEY isn't there at all. Check the image's build history to see how the Dockerfile handled it.
steps.fake_output:
CREATED BY
CMD ["node" "server.js"]
COPY . .
ARG API_KEY
FROM node:20-alpine
steps.hint: Notice there's an ARG instruction but no matching ENV instruction.

steps.prompt: ARG only exists at build time — it never becomes a runtime variable on its own. Pass it at runtime instead (the correct approach for a secret anyway).
steps.hint: -e sets an environment variable for the running container, which is what the app actually reads.

resolution: ARG values exist only during 'docker build' and disappear once the image is built — the running container never sees them unless the Dockerfile explicitly copies the value into an ENV instruction. But for a SECRET like an API key, baking it into the image via ENV would be worse: anyone who can pull the image can read it with 'docker history' or 'docker inspect'. The right fix is exactly what was done — pass secrets at RUNTIME with -e (or better, an env file or a secrets manager), never at build time. This is one of the most common real Dockerfile mistakes, and it has both a correctness failure mode (value missing) and a security failure mode (value leaked into the image) depending on which way someone tries to 'fix' it.
